meta.title: Classic Compute Plane: Rebuilt Posture, Not Just Topology

views.label: Control-plane link
views.note: Private Link, PrivateLink, or PSC — every cloud's name for the same requirement: no public internet to the control plane.

views.label: Egress control
views.note: Explicit allow-lists per endpoint, not a lifted 'allow all' from a source environment that had tighter rules.

views.label: What this plane doesn't cover
views.note: Serverless is on by default and governed by a separate account-level object — see serverless networking.

cards.title: Match posture, not just topology
items: The goal isn't 'a VPC exists' — it's no public IPs, private control-plane connectivity, and explicit egress, matching source exactly
A partial Private Link / PrivateLink setup silently falls back to public connectivity for the endpoint you missed
GCP requires explicit PSC endpoints per workspace — confirm DNS resolves to the private endpoint, not the public one

cards.title: Egress is enumerated, not inherited
items: Lifting 'allow all egress' from a looser source environment is a regression, not a migration
Every external endpoint workloads actually call comes from the asset inventory, allow-listed individually
Metastore and storage traffic route through private endpoints even when public would technically work

cards.title: Serverless isn't on this diagram for a reason
items: Serverless compute doesn't run in your VPC, so none of these controls govern it
It's on by default in new workspaces — a target can run workloads ungoverned while this network is still being built
Its egress is a separate account-level object: see serverless networking
